title: Two logic gates can add bits, and chained together they add numbers
body: A **half adder** adds two binary digits with just two logic gates: an XOR gate gives the sum bit, on when exactly one input is on, and an AND gate gives the carry, on when both are. A **full adder** also takes a carry in, and can be built from two half adders and an OR gate. Line full adders up side by side and each carry ripples into the next column, just like carrying digits when you add by hand. This ripple-carry adder is simple but relatively slow, because each stage has to wait for the carry from the one before.

slides.prompt: 5 is 0101 in binary and 3 is 0011. What is 5 + 3 in binary?
slides.detail: That's 8: one 8, no 4s, no 2s and no 1s. Every column produces a carry that moves one place left.

slides.alt: Animation on a green circuit board: an XOR and an AND gate add 1 + 1 to give 10, two half adders and an OR gate form a full adder, and four full adders in a row add 0101 + 0011 as glowing carries ripple from right to left, giving 1000, or 8.

slides.prompt: Tap the bits to set two numbers and watch the carries. Find a sum where a carry ripples all the way across, like 5 + 3.
slides.takeaway: Each column waits for the carry from its right before it can settle, so in a ripple-carry adder the slowest sums are the ones that carry the whole way.

slides.question: In a half adder, when does the AND gate switch the carry on?
slides.explanation: Only 1 + 1 overflows a single bit, giving binary 10. Exactly one 1 is the XOR gate's job: that's when the sum bit is on.

steps.label: A first half adder adds bits A and B
A second adds that sum to the carry in
An OR gate joins the two carries
Out come a sum bit and a carry out

slides.heading: Why rippling is slow
slides.text: Each full adder must wait for the carry from its neighbour, so a 32-bit ripple-carry adder waits on a chain of 32 of them. Faster designs, such as the carry-lookahead adder, work out the carries in advance.

slides.heading: An early adder
slides.text: In 1937, George Stibitz built a 2-bit binary adder, the Model K. In a ripple-carry adder, the first full adder can be swapped for a half adder, since nothing carries into the first column.
